learning: Compare line_loss_events, max_error, progress and completion on the s-bend and slalom with iteration 0. If oscillation rises while losses fall, reduce kd or kp slightly. If losses stay above about 1, the next step is the geometry change in entityR1 (span 0.08 m or narrower pitch).
notes: Adopts the Builder's 60 mm / 16 mm / y = 0.03 array. Gains are rescaled (kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45) so the steering response per metre of offset matches iteration 0 despite the wider span. Measurements compare directly with iteration 0.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the baseline (40 mm span, 12 mm footprints, y = 0.05, kp 4, ki 0.2, kd 0.3, base 1.5). The race ended off-track in 59 of 60 trials. Max_error averaged 0.063 to 0.065 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stayed small (0.016 to 0.022 m). The robot therefore tracks well on average and fails in transients. Line-loss events averaged 1.35 to 1.9 per run, highest on the slalom. Oval finish time was 1.73 s, so speed and drivetrain are not the limit. I keep the Builder's geometry unchanged so the test isolates the sensing change: 60 mm span, 15 mm pitch, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.03. The controller must adapt to this geometry. Weights are capped at ±2, so I keep (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2). The wider span means the signal changes by about 2/3 as much per metre of offset, so I raise kp from 4 to 6 to hold the effective steering gain near iteration 0. For the same reason I scale kd from 0.3 to 0.45 and ki from 0.2 to 0.3. The shorter lead (y = 0.03) reduces phase lag, so kd is not raised further. base_speed stays at 1.5 because the oval finished in 1.73 s and the 3 s limit is not the constraint. line_loss stays last_direction, since the new array should make losses rare and the search direction then matters less.
